messages:
marta: heads-up — onboarding sample failing for a customer on Node 14. stack trace points at require('redwood-sdk') throwing 'Cannot find module'.
kevin: ugh. which sample app/version?
sophie: @marta which package version are they using? export map changes recently could break require-based consumers.
marta: sample-app-js (the quickstart). they installed latest sdk@v6. package.json now uses conditional exports only (import/require subpaths) and we've removed the legacy 'main' fallback. repro: `node14 ./examples/quickstart/index.js` -> throws.
aron: Node14's resolver needs a plain main entrypoint if conditional exports don't include bare import for require. Did we include "./dist/index.cjs" under "require"?
marta: package.json exports: "{ ".": { "import": "./dist/index.mjs", "default": "./dist/index.cjs" } }" — note: no explicit `require` key. looks fine on Node 16+ but older consumer chains (metro, electron, some bundlers) still call require resolver path.
kevin: that default fallback is supposed to cover require but some older Node versions don't honor it or bundlers ignore conditional exports entirely. Also ts typings are pointing to types/index.d.ts but the distributed package only has types in `dist/types`. So types break for users importing `redwood-sdk` in TS projects.
sophie: we saw a similar mismatch in the edge runtime samples — edge bundlers (esbuild with "target: 'es2020'") prefer the import field; if runtime strips .mjs it can still work. But quickstart is CommonJS example so it should keep a CJS fallback.
ci-bot: CI failing: sample-app-js / install-and-smoke-test (linux-node14) — exit code 1. See logs: `Error: Cannot find module 'redwood-sdk'`
aron: quick fix: add explicit `require` key in exports and add top-level `main` pointing to `dist/index.cjs`. Also publish types at the top-level with `types: "dist/index.d.ts"`.
marta: +1. Can we also add a tiny note in the quickstart readme that the sample uses Node 14 CommonJS and to use node16+ for ESM-first flow?
kevin: I'll open a PR: add `main`, `require` export, and copy `dist/index.d.ts` to `dist/index.cjs.d.ts` (or better: set types to dist/index.d.ts). Also add a tiny smoke test in CI for node14.
sophie: long-term we should decide if we support Node14 at all for the quickstarts. maybe mark Node14 as deprecated but keep CJS fallback for a transition window. Also add a tsconfig example with "moduleResolution": "bundler" for ESM consumers to avoid ambiguous typings.\marta: thanks. I've pinged customer with workaround (use sdk@v5 or run example with node16). assigning kevin for PR. :thumbsup:
kevin: working on it now, will add tests and a short changelog note.
aron: also add a tiny repro in devex channel for future searches: `node -e "require('redwood-sdk')"` on Node14 should be part of smoke tests.
sophie: and maybe one-liner in API docs: "If you import with require() on Node <16, ensure package main/require fields exist or upgrade."
ci-bot: PR pipeline triggered: redwood/sdk#432 — node14-smoke-fix
marta: perfect. closing the loop here.
